canonical_industry_source: Must equal one of the canonical `industry` strings already governed in src/finengine/catalog.py's GROUPS industry scope_value and documented in docs/MASTER_SCHEMA.md (e.g. 'Banks', 'Telecommunications'), so a company's existing reviewed industry classification is what selects this pack — no new classification taxonomy is introduced.
notes: sector_specific_fields is not_applicable for telecom in this pack: telecom has no distinct sector-specific statement template in src/finengine/catalog.py comparable to banking's Basel III/IFRS 9 rows or insurance's IFRS 17 rows -- its subscriber/ARPU/churn metrics are physical operating-unit KPIs and belong entirely in operational_kpis, not sector_specific_fields. This mirrors catalog.py's own 'telecommunications' GROUPS entry, which only defines telecom_operations fields, no telecom-specific balance-sheet/income/ratio group.

ARPU and churn are frequently not disclosed even by large issuers -- docs/data/telecom-sector.md records 'stc does not publish ARPU in the reviewed 2021-2025 reports and no proxy is invented' and 'Zain's 2023-2024 5G-specific coverage is not disclosed separately'. Both are legitimate `unavailable` (reason: not_disclosed) outcomes under this pack, never a fabricated estimate.

5G/network coverage figures must be extracted only when the issuer's stated basis is unambiguous -- docs/data/telecom-sector.md explicitly excluded Mobily's ambiguous '99% coverage' figures for this reason. This is why operational_kpis.extraction_mode is requires_review at the master-contract level, not overridden per sector.
